subject: dads who coach little league
tagline: Home Depot for dads who coach little league
one_liner: A big-box supply store for volunteer coaches, where the batting order is sold by the linear foot and parent complaints go to the returns desk.
brand_voice_notes: Written like a contractor-grade retailer that has never met a nine-year-old. Every coaching problem is treated as a materials problem: lineups are lumber, morale is a load-bearing wall, and snack duty is a supply chain. Prices are stated plainly. Aisle numbers are specific. Nobody at Fungo has ever asked why a dad needs a pallet of orange slices, and nobody will.

hero.h1: Build the lineup. Pour the dugout. Be home by six.
hero.sub: Fungo stocks everything a volunteer coach needs for a Saturday, from pressure-treated batting orders to a returns desk that accepts parents. Aisle 14 has the clipboards. Aisle 14 has always had the clipboards.

features.title: Lineups, cut to length
features.blurb: Tell us how many kids showed up. Our in-store saw rips a batting order to size while you wait, pressure-treated against parents who have opinions about the three-hole. Offcuts go to the bench.

features.title: The parent returns desk
features.blurb: Bring your complaint to the orange counter with the original receipt. Gary will say he needs to check in the back. Gary has been checking in the back since 2019 and the complaint rate at partner fields has dropped 41 percent.

features.title: Orange slices, contractor pricing
features.blurb: Halftime citrus sold by the pallet and delivered by forklift to the gate behind Field 3. Every order is pre-quartered, logged to a SKU and backed by a 90-day freshness warranty we have never had to honor.

pricing_tiers.name: Weekend Project
pricing_tiers.tagline: For the dad who said yes at the parents' meeting because nobody else raised a hand.
perks: Access to the clipboard aisle on weekdays

pricing_tiers.name: Pro Desk
pricing_tiers.tagline: For coaches who have started calling it 'the program.'
perks: Priority lane at the parent returns desk
Your name embroidered on an apron

pricing_tiers.name: General Contractor
pricing_tiers.tagline: For the dad who also runs the snack bar and has keys to the equipment shed.
perks: A second adult who stands near you and nods

testimonials.quote: I used to do the lineup on the back of a gas receipt. Now it arrives on a pallet with a SKU and my wife says I talk about it too much at dinner.
testimonials.name: Doug Pressler
testimonials.title: Head Coach, Tri-County Hornets 8U; Regional Sales Manager, Mid-Atlantic Adhesives

testimonials.quote: The returns desk took a complaint about my son's playing time from my own brother-in-law. He was issued store credit. We have not discussed it since.
testimonials.name: Ray Okafor
testimonials.title: Assistant Coach, Lakeview Mudcats 10U; Owns Two Leaf Blowers

testimonials.quote: Forty pounds of orange slices, quartered, at the gate at 9:15. The forklift driver wished the kids luck. It is the most supported I have felt as a man.
testimonials.name: Brent Vasquez-Hollis
testimonials.title: Head Coach, Pine Hollow Pirates Coach-Pitch; Snack Bar Treasurer, Second Term

demo_screen_concept: The Lineup Builder, styled as a big-box store aisle inventory screen. Eleven kids from the Tri-County Hornets are listed as shelf SKUs with stock status (In stock = at practice, Backordered = at grandma's, Special order = at a birthday party) and spec fields like arm rating and 'attention span, minutes.' Filter chips by aisle (Infield, Outfield, Bench, Snack Duty) and a SKU search narrow the shelf. Clicking 'Add to lineup' moves a kid into a nine-slot batting order cart on the right, which can be reordered with up/down buttons. A 'Parent Friction Estimate' meter recalculates on every change, and 'Check out' opens a receipt modal that prints the lineup as a store receipt with a return policy for parents.

design_direction.style: Big-box retail wayfinding on a pegboard wall, fluorescent daylight mode. The page is staged as the inside of a warehouse hardware store: sealed concrete floor as the page ground, perforated brown hardboard pegboard panels for the hero and pricing wall, hanging double-sided aisle signs as section headers, and yellow shelf-edge price tags for every figure. One light mode only. Explicitly absent, because the previous seven entries used them: cork, push pins, tape strips, bites, egg-pulp cells, grade stamps, vent holes, vinyl bladders, valves, weld seams, chenille, brass plates, holographic foil, acrylic slabs, enamel plaques, terrazzo, galvanized zinc, rivets, hazard chevrons. Also absent: glassmorphism, blur, neon, dark mode, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The pegboard: #B98B5A hardboard with a regular 24px grid of 6px holes in #6E4F30, used only on the hero panel and the pricing wall, never behind body text without an opaque card. (2) The aisle sign: section headers sit on a hard-edged #1F3A5F panel hung from two thin 2px chain lines, carrying a huge aisle number in orange and the section name in white caps. (3) The shelf tag: every price, stat and SKU is Space Mono on a clearance-yellow #F5D430 tag with a 2px ink rule on top, a fake barcode strip in pure CSS repeating-linear-gradient, and unit pricing in small type underneath. (4) The apron: the primary CTA and the highlighted tier are apron orange #E2621B with ink text, square corners, and a stitched 1px dashed inner border. Headings are Archivo Black in caps, tight. Body is Archivo 17px/1.6. Everything numeric is Space Mono. Corners are square everywhere, radius 0 to 2px. Shadows are single hard 4px drops at 18 percent ink, like product on a shelf.
design_direction.archetype: Retail ecommerce landing with product-shelf composition: hero on pegboard, aisle-signed feature shelves, testimonial receipts, pricing as a pegboard wall of hanging price tags.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Shelf motion only: tags swing in with a 4 degree rotate settling to 0 on reveal, buttons press down 2px with the hard shadow shrinking to 2px, aisle signs sway once by 1 degree on hover. 180ms ease-out, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. Reveals are gated behind a .js class with a timeout fallback.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two-column hero on a pegboard panel. Left: an orange aisle marker 'AISLE 14 / COACHING SUPPLY', the h1 in huge Archivo Black caps on an opaque concrete card, sub, apron CTA and a secondary 'open the demo' link. Right: the hero photograph of a coach in a store aisle framed like a product on a hanging hook card, with a yellow shelf tag overlapping its bottom-left corner reading the price of the program. Collapses to one column under 900px.
